direction: Use a lexicographic de-jamming/feasibility-pump objective instead of directly minimising the maximum: fix a target $t$ slightly below the incumbent (e.g. $0.0663$, then $0.0660$, $0.0655$), and minimise $\sum_{i<j}\mathrm{softplus}_\beta(\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-t)^2$ restricted to pairs with cosine above $t-0.01$, with Riemannian Adam and $\beta$ annealed upward, explicitly trying to drive the number of pairs above the old maximum down to zero at that $t$ rather than shaving all tied pairs equally. direction: Search a symmetry-constrained fresh basin based on $58=2\times29$: parametrise two orbits of 29 points under a common orthogonal action of the cyclic group $C_{29}$ decomposed into eleven $2\times2$ rotation blocks on $\mathbb R^{22}$, where one orbit is generated from a seed vector by successive block rotations through multiples of $2\pi/29$ and the second orbit uses an independent seed (optionally with a fixed relative block-phase offset), so the whole code is described by only two seed vectors plus phases. Optimise this low-dimensional parametrisation with Adam on a sharply annealed log-sum-exp of all pairwise cosines to exploit the exact contact multiplicities a symmetric optimum would have, then release all $58\times22$ coordinates, quench, LP-polish, and compare against the incumbent; include several random seeds and phase choices under a strict 150s budget.

idea: Diverse softmax-quench population with contact-fingerprint archiving and Hungarian-Procrustes recombination plus final LP polish.
direction: Build a small population of genuinely diverse local optima and recombine them: generate about 16--24 fast softmax quenches from random starts and from differently perturbed copies of the record, aborting any run whose maximum cosine exceeds $0.09$ after a short burn-in, polish survivors only briefly, and fingerprint each by its sorted contact-degree sequence and the spectrum of its contact graph to keep an archive of non-isomorphic basins. idea: Alternate Gram clipping to target t below the record with PSD rank-22 projection from perturbed starts, then extract, softmax-quench and LP-polish the best Gram candidates.
direction: Attack the problem in Gram-matrix space rather than through tangent displacements by attempting feasibility at targets \(t\) equal to the record minus \(10^{-5},2\times10^{-5},5\times10^{-5}\), and \(10^{-4}\): starting from the incumbent Gram matrix, alternate between clipping all off-diagonal entries to at most \(t\) with diagonal fixed at one and projecting onto the positive-semidefinite rank-at-most-22 cone by retaining the 22 largest nonnegative eigenvalues, using several random perturbations of the initial Gram matrix. When the projection residual becomes small, extract vectors from the leading eigenvectors, normalize them, quench them with soft-max descent, and finish with LP polishing; this can change many contacts simultaneously and discover Gram spectra inaccessible to local trust-region steps.

Escape the jammed basin along collective low-stress modes of the active-contact Jacobian, walking until a new pair becomes maximal and re-quenching plus trust-region LP polishing.
direction: Escape along collective null modes of the jammed contact network: build tangent bases $B_i$ ($22\times21$) for each point, assemble the sparse active-contact Jacobian $A$ whose row for a contact $(i,j)$ within $10^{-7}$ of the maximum is $[(x_j-cx_i)^TB_i,\ (x_i-cx_j)^TB_j]$, and compute its 10--20 smallest right singular vectors with `scipy.sparse.linalg.svds`. Take finite steps of size $0.05$--$0.3$ along random combinations of these low-stress modes, retracting to the sphere and stopping when a previously inactive pair reaches the current maximum (a genuine topology change) or the maximum rises by a preset amount, then re-polish with the LP and record the new contact graph. This replaces per-point noise, which the LP reverses, with coordinated motions that the jam permits, and it directly targets the mechanism keeping the current optimum locked.

Dual-stress hub excision with greedy 20k-hole reinsertion and lexicographic acceptance
direction: Perform dual-stress-guided contact-graph surgery on the incumbent instead of random kicks: run the LP polish, extract HiGHS dual marginals for the active pairs as equilibrium stresses, rank points by total incident stress, and delete the 3--6 highest-stress hub points that lock the jam. Reinsert them jointly and greedily in the largest spherical holes: sample at least 20,000 candidate directions (random plus locally optimized hole maximizers minimizing the maximum dot product against the retained points), insert the best candidate, re-optimize the hole for the next deleted point against the updated set, then apply a short (200--400 step) annealed soft-max quench and a capped LP polish. Accept a surgery only on a lexicographic criterion that first counts pairs above targets such as $0.066$, $0.064$, and $0.060$, then compares the soft-max value, so progress is measured by losing stressed contacts, not merely by re-tying them at a microscopically lower maximum.
